basis: Required facts, each actual claim, each citation and all strict checks; literal matches and expected execution paths remain diagnostics.

semantic_labels.supported: All material subject, value, unit, date, source, modality, polarity and active-branch requirements are satisfied; equivalent phrasing and valid alternative evidence are accepted.
semantic_labels.partial: A material part is missing or only partly supported; a known strict failure.
semantic_labels.unsupported: The required fact is absent or its own cited evidence does not support it; a known strict failure.
semantic_labels.contradicted: The answer contradicts the authoritative source or applicable condition; a known strict failure.
semantic_labels.unclear: Available review evidence or annotation does not establish a decision; retain pending, not an invented pass or failure.

strict_definition: True only when every material required fact, actual claim, citation, strict check, expected answer status, execution/safety condition and mechanical binding is supported. A definite failed requirement yields false; otherwise any unresolved required review yields null. Missing annotation or unobserved answers are null, irrespective of model predictions.
conclusion_requirement: no_critical_error includes the final yes/no/unclear decision, its consistency with the body, complete response to the question, and correction of false premises. Correct direction alone does not establish strict success.
binding_boundary: Literal occurrence is a mechanical requirement, not semantic entailment. Valid cited premise chains can span claims; unrelated evidence elsewhere in context cannot repair the answer.
unknown_telemetry: Unknown token counters and incomplete full-run totals are null; measured subtotals and observed denominators are explicit. Actual zero counters remain zero. Failed calls and failed positions remain in cost/latency scope when observed.
latency: Recorded per-task wall latency, P50 median, P95 nearest-rank; disclose observed/total positions and background load. Never infer latency or cause from token totals.
human_annotation: First pass receives questions and complete actual sources only, without existing reference answers, model predictions, method names, experiment groups or expected experimental conclusions. Two independent human passes and explicit disagreements/adjudication are recorded; preparation is not completion.
provenance: Human-confirmed, model-assisted, pending and unknown are distinct. Model judgments never become human gold. Independence requires actual reviewer declarations, not anonymous identifiers or a different model alone.
history: Preserve old inputs, answers, annotations, judgments and reports. New protocol/reports are versioned; no post-Core changes to methods or thresholds.
third_party_text: Question, answer, source text and review reasons stay in ignored local directories. Public outputs contain hashes, IDs, counts, status and derived diagnostics only.
